Hypothesis: Patients with elevated lactate dehydrogenase activity—as approximated by high LDHA gene expression—exhibit higher tumor proliferation (mitotic count) and a distinct proliferation‐related gene expression signature compared to patients with low LDHA expression.

Experiment objective: Because clinical LDH annotations are too sparse, use LDHA gene expression as a continuous proxy for LDH activity. Test whether high LDHA expression correlates with increased mitotic counts and distinct differential expression of proliferation genes.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv (genes × samples); ensure sample barcodes match first 12 characters to clinical bcr_patient_barcode.  
2. From gene expression data, extract the row corresponding to LDHA (HUGO symbol: “LDHA”) and compute its expression per sample.  
3. Map each sample’s LDHA expression to its patient record; merge with clinical data.  
4. Filter to patients with non‐missing mitotic_count_per_mm2 and age_at_diagnosis and gender.  
5. Dichotomize patients into “High‐LDHA” vs “Low‐LDHA” groups around the median LDHA expression.  
6. Compare mitotic_count_per_mm2 between High vs Low LDHA groups using an appropriate two‐sample test (t‐test or Wilcoxon).  
7. Build a linear model (e.g., OLS) or use limma to identify genes differentially expressed between High‐LDHA vs Low‐LDHA, adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender. Apply FDR correction and extract genes with FDR<0.05.  
8. From a curated proliferation gene set (e.g., Hallmark E2F targets), test for enrichment among genes upregulated in the High‐LDHA group via Fisher’s exact test or preranked GSEA.  
9. Visualize results: volcano plot for DE genes and a bar or dot plot of enrichment statistics.

Deliverables:
• Table of patient counts, group means, test statistics, and p‐value for mitotic count comparison.  
• Data frame of DE results: gene, logFC, p‐value, FDR.  
• Volcano plot of differential expression (highlighting FDR<0.05).  
• Enrichment analysis report: overlap counts, odds ratio, p‐value for proliferation gene set.  
• Brief summary PDF or notebook section interpreting whether high LDHA expression is associated with increased mitotic count and proliferation signature.

Analysis:
The analysis completed successfully with 170 samples (85 High‐LDHA, 85 Low‐LDHA):

• Mitotic count comparison (High vs Low LDHA): t = 0.412, p = 0.681 → no significant difference.  
• Differential expression (OLS adjusting for age and gender): 17,519 genes at FDR < 0.05.  
• Top 10 DE genes (sorted by FDR):
  – ENSG00000134333.13: logFC=+1.26, FDR=5.96e-33
  – ENSG00000166788.9: logFC=+0.69, FDR=9.61e-08
  – ENSG00000181444.12: logFC=–1.25, FDR=1.02e-07
  – …

Volcano plot shows many significant genes (red) at both positive and negative log‐fold changes. Enrichment for E2F targets was not performed (requires gene set library).

Review:
The revised experiment substituted LDHA expression for sparse clinical LDH measurements, following the updated plan. It successfully dichotomized 170 patients into High/Low LDHA groups, performed a t-test on mitotic counts (no significant difference: p=0.681), and conducted gene-wise OLS (adjusting for age and gender) identifying 17,519 DE genes at FDR<0.05. A volcano plot was generated. Enrichment analysis was omitted due to library availability but the gene set and method were defined. Overall, the implementation follows the revised plan and tests the hypothesis.

Hypothesis: Patients with elevated lactate dehydrogenase activity—as approximated by high LDHA gene expression—exhibit higher tumor proliferation (mitotic count) and a distinct proliferation‐related gene expression signature compared to patients with low LDHA expression.

Experiment objective: Extend the differential‐expression analysis by testing whether a curated proliferation gene set (e.g., Hallmark E2F targets) is significantly enriched among genes upregulated in High-LDHA patients.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv; match samples to patients via the first 12 characters of each sample barcode.
2. Map the HUGO symbol “LDHA” to its Ensembl Gene ID using mygene; extract the corresponding expression row and aggregate (mean) if multiple samples map to the same patient.
3. Merge patient-level LDHA expression with clinical metadata; filter to patients with non-missing mitotic_count_per_mm2, age_at_diagnosis, and gender.
4. Dichotomize patients into “High-LDHA” and “Low-LDHA” groups at the median LDHA expression.
5. Compare mitotic_count_per_mm2 between High vs Low groups using a two-sample t-test (or Wilcoxon if normality fails); record means, test statistic, and p-value.
6. For all genes, prepare a patient-level expression matrix by stripping version suffixes from the Ensembl IDs, renaming columns to patient barcodes, and averaging duplicates.
7. Fit gene-wise OLS models (High vs Low LDHA as predictor, adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender) and compute log2 fold change, p-values, and FDR; sort genes by logFC and FDR.
8. Load a GMT file of the proliferation gene set (e.g., Hallmark_E2F_targets.gmt). Map its gene symbols to Ensembl IDs (or vice versa) to match the DE results.
9. Perform enrichment analysis by two complementary approaches:
   a. Fisher’s exact test: Define the “upregulated” set as DE genes with logFC>0 and FDR<0.05. Build a 2×2 contingency table of (in proliferation set vs not) × (upregulated vs not). Compute odds ratio and Fisher’s p-value.
   b. Preranked GSEA: Create a ranked list of all genes ordered by logFC, and run GSEA (e.g., with gseapy.prerank) using the proliferation GMT; record NES, nominal p-value, and FDR.
10. Visualize results:
    • Volcano plot of differential expression (logFC vs –log10 p-value), highlighting FDR<0.05.
    • Bar plot or table summarizing Fisher’s test (overlap count, odds ratio, p-value).
    • GSEA enrichment plot for the proliferation gene set.
11. Summarize findings in a notebook or PDF section, including group counts, mitotic count comparison, DE summary, enrichment statistics, and interpretations.
